correctness.rationale: With the stated shift convention the projector Gram is the convolution kernel |A(h,w)|² at h=a−c,w=b−d. For the character (a,b)↦ζ_N^(ua+vb), expanding the ambiguity square and summing over w sets the two sample indices a lag v apart; the h-transform factors as a modulus square. This gives N|A(−v,u)|² at the stated label, not only as an unordered spectrum. Fourier-character kernel directions of the projector Gram correspond to zero weights, while Weyl operator directions describe the intensity-lifting kernel. Centering s=t+h/2 gives 4hs³+(h³−w)s+wh/2. Modulo p, cyclotomic irreducibility makes exact cancellation equivalent to the cubic being a permutation. For nonzero linear coefficient b in ax³+bx, the off-diagonal collision conic u²+3v²=−4b/a has p−χ(−3) solutions (count the quadratic character by a split difference of squares), at most two with u=0; for p≥5 this forces a collision. For b=0, cyclicity gives the p≡2 mod 3 condition. Modulo p², the two-digit split leaves exactly the stationary residue contributions, without a simple-root restriction. For unit h there are zero, one or two such residues; two p²-th roots cannot cancel at odd p. For h=pH≠0 only w=pW can survive and the residue sum is exactly the already classified cubic 4Hx³−Wx. The h=0 row is orthogonality. Counting 1, then (p−1)(p−δ_p), then (p²−p)p(p+1)/2 gives the square-order rank, and the h=0 and nonzero-shift zeros give the prime-order rank. The frozen checker’s floating comparisons sort spectra and do not by themselves test labels. Independent replay /workspace/branches/frozen-review-replay.py checks unsorted character-by-character values from the first Gram row and checks exact exponent-histogram cancellations for p=5,7 at both orders; ranks 17,43,317,1219 and worst labeled error below 1.5e−14. The analytic classification, not finite evidence, proves all p≥5.
